title: Klaipėdos miesto savivaldybės želdynų ir želdinių inventorizavimo paslaugos.
description: Klaipėdos miesto savivaldybės želdynų ir želdinių inventorizavimo paslaugos. Tiekėjo pasiūlymo kaina negali viršyti 60 000,00 Eur su PVM (arba 49 586,78 Eur be PVM, jei tiekėjas yra ne PVM mokėtojas ar paslaugos neapmokestinamos PVM, ar dėl kitų priežasčių, dėl kurių Perkančiosios organizacijos galutinė tiekėjui mokėtina suma bus be PVM), šią sumą viršijantys pasiūlymai bus laikomi nepriimtinais ir bus atmetami. Preliminarūs perkamų paslaugų kiekiai nurodyti konkurso sąlygų aprašo 1 priede, jie Sutarties vykdymo metu pagal Perkančiosios organizacijos poreikį gali būti mažinami arba gali būti didinami. Maksimaliai paslaugų gali būti užsakoma už ne daugiau kaip 60 000,00 Eur su PVM (arba 49 586,78 Eur be PVM, jei tiekėjas yra ne PVM mokėtojas ar paslaugos neapmokestinamos PVM, ar dėl kitų priežasčių, dėl kurių Perkančiosios organizacijos galutinė tiekėjui mokėtina suma bus be PVM). Išsamesnė perkamų paslaugų informacija ir reikalavimai pateikiami techninėje specifikacijoje ir jos priede (konkurso sąlygų aprašo 3 priedas). Šis pirkimas į dalis neskaidomas, todėl tiekėjas turi pateikti pasiūlymą visai pirkimo apimčiai bendrai.

title: Belgium – Guard services – Marché portant sur des services de gardiennage pour Wallonie Bruxelles International (WBI) et l’Agence wallonne à l’Exportation et aux Investissements étrangers (AWEX)
description: L’objet du marché est la prestation de services relatifs à des services de gardiennage et porte notamment sur : • La surveillance des bâtiments et la protection des agents qui y travaillent ; • La surveillance à distance des bâtiments conformément au programme des prestations tel que détaillé dans la partie relative aux exigences techniques du Cahier spécial des charges, ci-après dénommé « CSC » ; • L’ouverture et la fermeture des accès des bâtiments, en ce compris l’activation et la désactivation des alarmes ; • L’accueil et l’identification des visiteurs ; • La réception de colis, de services ou fournitures en l’absence d’agent ; • La permanence du central téléphonique ; • La réalisation de rondes de sécurité à l’extérieur des bâtiments les weekends, les jours fériés et jour de dispense ; • L’intervention rapide en cas de déclenchement d’une alarme, quelle qu’elle soit, ou en cas de panne ; • La prise de contact avec des prestataires techniques désignés en cas constat de toute anomalie technique dans l’un des bâtiments, et la rédaction du compte rendu y relatif ; • L’information régulière au Pouvoir adjudicateur sur les évènements constatés à l’occasion de la réalisation des prestations ;

title: Germany – Engineering services – Technische Projekt- und Ingenieursleistungen
description: Die 50Hertz Transmission GmbH (nachfolgend Auftraggeber) schreibt Rahmenverträge für technische Projekt- und Ingenieursleistungen zur Umsetzung der AC, DC und Offshore Projekte in der Regelzone der 50Hertz aus. Die ausgeschriebenen Leistungen umfassen Bau- und Infrastrukturtechnik, Elektrotechnische Anlagen und Systeme, Kabel- und Freileitungstechnik, Baugrunduntersuchung und Kampfmittelentsorgung, Fachbauleitung, Bauoberleitung und Bauüberwachung, Vermessung und Bestandsplanung, Trassierung von Erdkabeln, Qualitätssicherung und -kontrolle sowie Teilprojektleitung Freileitung/Umspannwerk. Ziel der Ausschreibung ist der Abschluss von mehreren Rahmenverträgen mit verschiedenen Auftragnehmern pro Los. Neben der 50Hertz Transmission GmbH sind alle mit der Elia Gruppe verbundenen Unternehmen (insbesondere 50Hertz Offshore GmbH, 50Hertz Connectors GmbH, Elia Grid International GmbH, Elia Transmission Belgium S.A., Elia Asset S.A. und Elia Engineering S.A.) berechtigt, diesen Vertrag in Anspruch zu nehmen. Darüber hinaus behält sich der Auftraggeber vor, diesen Vertrag auf aktuelle oder künftige verbundene Unternehmen oder Unternehmen, an den der Auftraggeber beteiligt ist, zu übertragen. Gleichermaßen bleibt dem Auftraggeber bei einer gesellschaftsrechtlichen Umstrukturierung des Auftragnehmers oder bei Wegfall einzelner Mitglieder eines Unternehmensverbunds (ARGE als AN) vorbehalten, den Vertrag auf den neuen Unternehmensträger oder verbleibende Mitglieder eines Unternehmensverbundes zu übertragen.

title: Family Support Services (Inverclyde)
description: Inverclyde Health and Social Care Partnership (HSCP) and the Inverclyde Alcohol and Drug Partnership (ADP) require the delivery of a Family Support Service (FSS) for adults and young people aged 16 years and over, who reside in Inverclyde and are affected by the alcohol and/or drug use of a family member, partner, friend or loved one. The Family Support service will recognise that substance use can have a significant and lasting impact on family members in their own right and that families require support regardless of whether their loved one is currently engaged in treatment, recovery or active substance use. The Family Support service will place families at the centre of all activity and will operate within a framework of: Trauma-Informed Practice Family Inclusive Practice Whole Family Approaches Human Rights Based Practice Recovery-Oriented Systems of Care The Family Support service will provide; early intervention, prevention, emotional support, education, advocacy, peer support, bereavement support, pathways for moving on to other community-based supports when appropriate, and family recovery interventions to improve outcomes for individuals, families and communities across Inverclyde.

title: Turvajärjestelmien huolto- ja ylläpitopalveluiden hankinta
description: Turvajärjestelmien huolto- ja ylläpitopalveluiden hankinta Hankinnan kohteena on Oulun yliopiston ja Oulun Ammattikorkeakoulu Oy:n (OAMK) turvajärjestelmien ylläpitopalvelu. Hankinnan tavoitteena on muodostaa Tilaajalle yhtenäinen toimintamalli turvajärjestelmien ylläpitoon, huoltoon, muutostöihin ja elinkaaren hallintaan. Hankinta koskee Tilaajan turvajärjestelmiä kaikissa sen kohteissa. Hankinnan piiriin kuuluvat myös sopimuskauden aikana käyttöönotettavat uudet kohteet sekä olemassa oleviin kohteisiin toteutettavat laajennukset ja muutokset. Tällä hetkellä Oulun yliopisto toimii ensisijaisena tilaajana ja läpilaskuttaa kustannukset Oulun Ammattikorkeakoululta (OAMK). Sopimuskauden aikana myös Oamkilla voi syntyä omia hankintatarpeita, jotka liittyvät esimerkiksi järjestelmien uudistamiseen tai korvaamiseen. Oulun yliopiston konsulttina tässä kilpailutuksessa toimii Seclion Oy. Hankinnan kuvaus tarkemmin liitteissä "Hankinnan yleiskuvaus" ja "Palvelukuvaus".,

title: Oulun Tilapalvelut - Hissien huolto- ja korjauspalvelut
description: Oulun Tilapalvelut - Hissien huolto- ja korjauspalvelut HANKINNAN KOHDE Oulun Tilapalvelut -liikelaitos pyytää tarjoustanne hallinnoimiensa kiinteistöjen hissien huolto- ja korjauspalveluista sekä hälytyskeskuspalveluista. Hankinnan kohteena ovat hissien kokonaisvaltainen huolto-, kunnossapito-, korjaus- ja päivystyspalvelu. Palveluun sisältyvät lisäksi hissien toiminnan ylläpitämiseksi tarvittavat muut huolto- ja korjaustoimenpiteet. Palvelun tavoitteena on varmistaa hissien turvallinen, luotettava ja keskeytyksetön toiminta sekä ylläpitää laitteiden tekninen kunto valmistajien ohjeiden, viranomaismääräysten ja hyvän kunnossapitotavan mukaisesti. Hankinnan tarkempi sisältö on kuvattu tämän tarjouspyynnön liitteessä 1 (Palvelunkuvaus). Lisäksi liitteessä 2, (Laiteluettelo / Tarjousliite) on kerrottu jokaisen hissin vaadittu huoltomäärä vuodessa. SOPIMUSJÄRJESTELY Hankinnasta muodostetaan puitejärjestely yhden (1) palveluntuottajan kanssa. TOIMEKSIANTOJEN TOTEUTUS Perushuollot toteutetaan sovitun huolto-ohjelman mukaisesti. Kiireettömien töiden tilaukset tehdään P2P-tilausjärjestelmällä, joka toimii samalla tilauksen sopimuksena. Tilauksen yhteydessä sovitaan toimeksiannon sisältö, aikataulu sekä arvioitu työmäärä. Mikäli sovitusta aikataulusta myöhästytään palveluntuottajasta johtuvasta syystä, tilaajalla on oikeus periä sopimusluonnoksen mukaiset sanktiot. HINNOITTELU JA TARJOUKSEN SISÄLTÖ Tarjous tulee laatia tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Tarjouksen tulee kattaa kaikki palvelun toteuttamiseksi tarvittavat työt. Mahdolliset lisätyöt hinnoitellaan tarjouspyynnön mukaisesti. Perushuollot laskutetaan laitekohtaisilla tarjoushinnoilla. Muut huolto- ja korjaustyöt laskutetaan tarjotun tuntihinnan sekä toteutuneen materiaalikulutuksen mukaisesti. SOPIMUSKAUSI Sopimuskausi on kaksi (2) vuotta. Sopimuskauden tavoiteltu alkamispäivä on 1.12.2026. Mikäli sopimuskauden aloitus viivästyy esimerkiksi muutoksenhaun vuoksi, sopimuskausi alkaa vasta, kun asiaan on saatu lainvoimainen ratkaisu. Määräaikaisen sopimuskauden jälkeen sopimusta voidaan jatkaa optioilla: - yksi (1) + yksi (1) vuotta Optiokaudet alkavat tavoitellusti: - 1.11.2028 (1. optiovuosi) - 1.11.2029 (2. optiovuosi) Tilaaja päättää optioiden käytöstä. Sopimus jatkuu optiokausille automaattisesti, ellei tilaaja ilmoita kirjallisesti halustaan olla käyttämättä optiota viimeistään kuusi (6) kuukautta ennen kunkin optiokauden alkamista. HISSIEN LISÄÄMINEN JA POISTAMINEN Sopimuskaudella hankinnan kohteet voivat lisääntyä tai vähentyä ja tilaajalla on oikeus lisätä tai poistaa kohteita sopimuksesta ilman irtisanomisaikaa. Lisättyihin ja poistettuihin kohteisiin sovelletaan tarjouksen mukaisia hintatasoja. TAKUUAIKAISTEN HISSIEN HUOLTOVASTUU Tämä hankinta ei koske takuuaikaisia huolto- ja korjauspalveluja. title: Ilmanpuhdistuslaitteiden vuokraus ja hankinta
description: Vantaan kaupunki pyytää tarjouksia ilmanpuhdistimien vuokraamisesta ja hankinnasta. Hankinnan kohteena ovat vuokrattavat ja ostettavat sisäilmanpuhdistuslaitteet julkisiin tiloihin, kuten koulu- ja päiväkotitiloihin, toimistoihin, arkistoihin, auditorioihin jne. Tilaajat hankkivat pääosin vuokrattavia laitteita, ja vähäisissä määrin laitteita tullaan ostamaan omaksi. Ilmanpuhdistimilla haetaan väliaikaista ratkaisua sisäilmaongelmien hallintaan käyttöä turvaavana toimenpiteenä. Ilmanpuhdistimien tulee olla tarkoitettu tähän käyttötarkoitukseen. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteellä 2 Palvelukuvaus. Kilpailutus suoritetaan avoimella menettelyllä, jonka perusteella jokaiseen osa-alueeseen puitetoimittajiksi valitaan kolme (3) vertailussa eniten pisteitä saanutta tarjoajaa etusijajärjestyksessä. Hankinta kilpailutetaan yhteishankintana niin, että Vantaan kaupunki julkaisee tarjouspyynnön. Kilpailutuksen perusteella tehdään samansisältöiset, sopimusluonnoksen (liite 1) mukaiset sopimukset Vantaan kaupungille, Kauniaisten kaupungille ja Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialueelle. Hankintayksiköt tekevät myös oman päätöksensä. Vantaan kaupungille tehtävien sopimusten perusteella hankintoja voivat tehdä Vantaan kaupungin kaikki toimialat sekä Vantaan Tilapalvelut Vantti Oy, VTK Kiinteistöt Oy- konserni, VAV Yhtymä Oy, VAV Asunnot Oy, VAV Palvelukodit Oy, VAV Hoiva-asunnot Oy, Hakopolun Liikekiinteistö Oy, Kiinteistö Oy Hakucenter, Kiinteistö Oy Vantaan Maakotkantie 10, Pallastunturintien Liikekiinteistö Oy ja Asunto Oy Vantaan Katriinanrinne. Sopimustoimittaja voi tarjota samoin ehdoin tuotteitaan ja palvelujaan Vantaan kaupungin seuraaville konsernitoimijoille: Vivamus Kiinteistöt Oy ja Kiinteistö Oy Vantaan Sote-tilat. Sopimuskausi on kaksi (2) vuotta, jonka jälkeen sopimusta voidaan jatkaa kahdella (2) yhden (1) vuoden optiolla (1+1). Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa ilmoitettuihin euromääräisiin arvoihin tai tiettyihin arvioituihin hankintamääriin sopimuskaudella., Osa-alue 1: Puhtaanilmantuotto 160 m3/h Ilmanpuhdistuslaitteiden vuokraus ja hankinta toimistotiloihin., Osa-alue 2: Puhtaanilmantuotto 400 m3/h Ilmanpuhdistinten vuokraus ja hankinta., Osa-alue 3: Puhtaanilmantuotto 800 m3/h Ilmanpuhdistinten vuokraus ja hankinta isoihin tiloihin.,

title: France – Repair and maintenance services of electrical and mechanical building installations – Conduite et maintien en conditions opérationnelles des installations de courant fort, courant faible, courant faible de sécurité et des équipements électromécaniques des centres du CEA/DAM
description: Le périmètre du marché couvre les activités relatives à la conduite et au maintien en conditions opérationnelles en vue d’assurer la disponibilité et la sécurité des installations de courant fort, de courant faible, de courant faible de sécurité et des équipements électromécaniques des centres CEA DAM. Elles incluent : — conduite (relevés et suivis de paramètres, vérifications, consignations/déconsignations, arrêt/redémarrage d’équipements, réglages nécessaires au fonctionnement de l’équipement,etc.) ; — maintenance préventive et contrôles et essais périodiques, mise en configuration du matériel pour VRP ; — dépannage ; — petits travaux (opérations mineures de modifications d’installations) ; — participation aux réceptions de chantier expertises ; — méthode (rédaction des gammes de maintenance, des modes opératoires, des documents de sécurité, des comptes-rendus d’interventions, la gestion de stocks, le REX terrain) ; — planification des interventions. L'avis de marché comporte 4 lots géographiques : - Lot 1 concerne les prestations pour le centre DIF (B26-06848) ; - Lot 2 concerne les prestations pour le centre de VALDUC (B26-06854) ; - Lot 3 concerne les prestations pour le centre du CESTA (B26-06855) ; - Lot 4 concerne les prestations pour le centre du RIPAULT (B26-06856).

title: Design and Construction of Levee Access Manholes for Fairfax-Jersey Creek Levee Unit (Kansas City, Kansas)
description: Levee Access Manholes for Fairfax-Jersey Creek Levee Unit. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District, has a need for design-build construction services to install access manholes to facilitate access to an existing seepage collection system in the levee. Invasive mass excavation methods such as trenching will not be allowed. Minimally invasive excavation methods are required. The location is the Fairfax-Jersey Creek Levee Unit on the Missouri River in Kansas City, Kansas. The requirements are described in more detail in this solicitation. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 237990, Size Standard $45 Million. The magnitude of this project is represented by the following estimated price range: Between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. THE CONTRACT AWARD AMOUNT (INCLUSIVE OF ALL CONTRACT LINE ITEMS) SHALL NOT EXCEED $3,400,000.00 FOR THIS PROJECT. OFFERORS ARE UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO APPROACH THIS AMOUNT.

title: CONTRACTOR-OPERATED PARTS STORE (COPARS)
description: To provide repair parts, replacement components, supplies, materials, equipment and services in support of automotive, forklift, heavy equipment, material handling, construction, and civil engineering equipment maintenance, via a staffed on-site parts store or contractor-owned consignment inventory, on-demand delivery service, or a combination of two or more methods. This effort supports the United States Marine Corps (USMC) Southwest Region Fleet Transportation (SWRFT) division, which consist of seven (7) sites throughout California and Arizona. SWRFT is responsible for the management, readiness, and operational support of vehicles and equipment that support Marine Corps installation commanders and tenant activities located in the Southwestern United States. The SWRFT consists of Southern California Region sites at Marine Corps Base (MCB) Camp Pendleton, CA; Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Miramar, CA; Marine Corps Recruit Depot (MCRD) San Diego, CA; Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center (MCAGCC), Twentynine Palms, CA; Marine Corps Logistics Base (MCLB) Barstow, CA; and Marine Corps Mountain Warfare Training Center (MCMWTC) Bridgeport, CA; as well as Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Yuma, AZ located outside the Southern California region.

title: Mosquito Lake Control Tower Structural Standing Seam Metal Roof Replacement
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District has a project that involves the complete replacement of the standing seam metal roof on the Control Tower Building at Mosquito Creek Lake in Cortland, Ohio. The work is to be completed within 365 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). Rough Estimate of this non-commercial construction project is between $150,000.00 and $350,000.00. The work includes rerouting existing vent and exhaust pipes through the masonry side wall, installing a new gutter system, and integrating a new, certified, non-penetrating Lightning Protection System. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) is 238160 - Roofing Contractors. The Small Business Size Standard is $19,000,000.00. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Contract. The Request for Quote (RFQ) will be issued on, or about, 4 September 2026, via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE), which posts the opportunity to SAM.gov. The anticipated award date is 13 November 2026. Basis of Award is best value to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with (IAW) RFO 12.203(a), price and past performance. The Government reserves the right to reject any quotes that are unrealistically low or exceed available funds for this requirement. Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and duration goals to achieve definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found by going to https://www.usace.army.mil/Strategic-Partnerships/Partnering/mod/129895/details/443/ then scrolling down on right hand side of page by clicking on View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here.

title: NGA HRM-II RFP
description: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) is to issue this Request for Proposal (RFP) HM047626R0018 for public response for the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) Human Resource Management II (HRM II). The HRM II RFP will be a commercial effort under FAR Part 12, and the Government anticipates using Best Value � Tradeoff evaluation methods and acquisition procedures as described in FAR Part 15. Contract award will be made to the offeror who provides the best overall value to the Government in terms of evaluation factors listed in Section 5 of the RFP. The procurement will be conducted using full and open competition procedures. The Government contemplates award of a performance-based contract using Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and Time-and-Materials (T&M) CLINs resulting from the solicitation. The period performance is anticipated to be a one (1) year base period with four (4) twelve (12) month option periods. The HRM II acquisition includes: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency requires comprehensive Human Resource Management support services across the employee lifecycle. The requirement includes support for functions such as personnel data processing, talent acquisition support, talent development support, strategic workforce planning, employee support services, performance records management, benefits processing, retirement tracking, and related HR management support activities. In order to be considered for this requirement, the offeror shall have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), https://www.sam.gov. Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://www.sam.gov. Registration MUST contain the appropriate North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 541612 � Human Resources Consulting Services Size Standard $29M. title: DUAL ENROLLMENT PARTNERSHIP OPPORTUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT
description: The Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) is seeking capability statements from eligible Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs) interested in establishing no-cost Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) or Memorandums of Agreement (MOAs) to support dual or concurrent enrollment opportunities for DoWEA students worldwide. This announcement seeks institutional, academic, financial, technical, cybersecurity, privacy, and programmatic information from IHEs to assess their capability to participate in a dual enrollment partnership program pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2164c. This announcement is not a solicitation for proposals, request for quotations, request for offers, grant opportunity, or procurement action, and no contract award is contemplated. Responses will be used solely to evaluate institutional capabilities and determine whether DoWEA may pursue discussions regarding one or more no-cost MOUs or MOAs. Submission of a response does not guarantee selection, discussions, execution of an agreement, student participation, enrollment volumes, or future opportunities. Any resulting MOU or MOA will be non-procurement in nature and will not obligate the Government to expend funds, pay tuition or fees, reimburse participants, refer students, guarantee enrollments, or enter into any agreement. DoWEA may select one, multiple, or no respondents and reserves the right to discontinue consideration of any response at any time. All interested IHEs should review the full announcement for eligibility requirements, submission instructions, and response deadlines. For more information, please see attachment 27R0001_DualEnroll_OA_092426

title: Calibration services for a diverse inventory of Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic
description: N0016426SNBXX REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT Calibration services for a diverse inventory of Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE) PSC J052, J066, H266, H366 NAICS 541380, 811219 1.0 Objective & Background This Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought (SS) notice is issued by the Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC), Crane Division Contracting Department, Crane, IN. The NSWC Crane Contracting Department is conducting market research to identify potential industry partners capable of providing comprehensive calibration services in accordance with OPNAV 3960.16 for a diverse inventory of Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE). Currently, NSWC Crane utilizes organic support in combination with a SeaPort Task Order and a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for calibration of TMDE for navy programs at NSWC Crane. The Government is exploring the feasibility of consolidating these requirements into a single, multi-year contract (e.g., Base Year plus Option Years). The primary objective of this market research is to determine if industry is interested in running the calibration program in accordance with the OPNAV 3960.16 at the contractor's own facility or government owned contractor ran facility. The Government is seeking capability statements regarding the calibration of approximately 2,700 unique TMDE types and ~7,000 total TMDE assets annually to ensure operational readiness and strict compliance with technical standards. 2.0 Acquisition Strategy & Disclaimer THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The Navy has not made a commitment to procure any of the items discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Information gathered from this market research will directly inform the Government's future acquisition strategy, including the determination of contract type, the feasibility of consolidating these calibration services, and the viability of shifting the primary place of performance to contractor-owned facilities. 3.0 Incumbent Contract Information The current workload is distributed across the following contract vehicles: Supported Equipment N0017819D8285/N0016423F3007 Goldbelt ILS 5/1/2023-4/30/2028 Unsupported Equipment N0016426A0026 Cross technologies 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 N0016426A0025 ENI 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 N0016426A0024 Transcat 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 N0016426A0023 Micro precision 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 N0016426A0022 Tektronix 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 4.0 Summary of Requirements The required calibration services span multiple asset categories. All calibration services must be performed in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025, navy approved and/or specialized approved procedures. Technical Standard & Location Requirements: The Government intends for the bulk of calibration services to be performed by the contractor at the contractor's facility. All calibrations must conform strictly to the ISO/IEC 17025 standard. While most calibration efforts will be conducted at contractor facilities and on station at NSWC Crane, there will be a significant amount of calibration workload that will be conducted at various industry locations supporting NSWC Crane workload. Locations vary across Indiana and adjoining states and are subject to change through the life of the contract. Logistics requirements: Personnel physically inspect the shipping container and the TMDE itself for transit damage. Onsite Pick up/delivery of assets 2-5 times per week Reference MIL-STD-2073-1 for assets over $10,000 Verifies that all components listed on the shipper's DD Form 1149 or stowage list are present. Engineering services: The Contractor shall provide high level support in Metrology and Calibration Laboratory for various project and programs at NSWC CRANE. Various Administration support: Contractors must maintain rigorous, auditable stewardship of all GFP throughout its lifecycle using the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) GFP Module. title: CAAA Rapid Acquisition Sustainment Program (RASP) BOA
description: SECTION A � SOLICITATION EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 1. THREE-STEP PROCUREMENT FRAMEWORK The Government will procure the Rapid Acquisition Sustainment Program (RASP) supply requirements utilizing a three-step process: Step One (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation): A separate Pre-solicitation Notice will not be issued; this synopsis is combined with the solicitation on SAM.gov in accordance with FAR Subpart 12.6. Individual order-level Request for Quotes (RFQs) under this Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) will be competed exclusively within the qualified pool and will not be synopsized, ensuring rapid execution. Clauses are in effect through FAC 2026-01. The primary NAICS code is 332710 (Machine Shops; Size Standard: 500 employees). Other codes are listed in Attachment 0001 - RASP BOA Purchase Description, and the Product Service Code is 5340 (Hardware, Commercial). Step Two (Master BOA Execution): The BOA Request for Proposal (RFP) will be released once for qualifications. The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors whose proposals are compliant with Section L and rated "Acceptable" under Section M. BOAs are valid for up to five (5) years. NOTE: This RFP is the only opportunity to obtain a RASP BOA. Proposals will not be accepted or executed at any other time. If a contractor wishes to participate in any future RASP orders, they must respond to this initial RFP. Step Three (Order-Level Competition): As recurring supply needs arise, the PCO will issue competitive, order-level RFQs to the BOA pool. To participate, contractors must hold an active master BOA as of the RFQ closing date. Orders will result in individual, competitive Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contracts (Orders) under FAR 16.703. 2. SCOPE Contractors will provide commercial products supporting Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA) operations across the categories defined in Section B. Items ordered may include detailed specifications from controlled technical data packages referencing military specifications (MIL-SPEC) or restricted technical drawings. 3. SUBCONTRACTING FLEXIBILITY Offerors must demonstrate technical capability within the scope of Attachment 0001- RASP BOA Purchase Description. Capability may be achieved with or without subcontractors. In Step Three order-level proposals, contractors are not bound to the subcontractors proposed in Step Two but must propose resources necessary to perform each individual order. 4. BASIS FOR AGREEMENT EXECUTION The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors with compliant proposals (Section L) rated "Acceptable" (Section M). NOTE: The Government reserves the right to waive the Compliance Review if in its best interest. The Government intends to execute BOAs on initial proposals without discussions. It reserves the right to negotiate if in its best interest but will only do so with offerors whose proposals do not contain significant informational deficiencies. LEGAL NOTICE: This master BOA process is not a competitive acquisition; the source selection procedures of FAR Part 15 do not apply. No pricing is requested or evaluated at this stage. Execution of a BOA does not constitute a contract or guarantee future orders. SECTION B � CONTRACT LINE ITEM NUMBERS (CLINS) The following unfunded CLINs are established at the master agreement level for administrative categorization only: CLIN 0001: Machined and Fabricated Metal Parts (NAICS 332710 / 332999) CLIN 0002: Plastics and Injection Molded Components (NAICS 326199) CLIN 0003: Wooden Containers, Boxes, and Pallets (NAICS 321920) CLIN 0004: Chemicals, Organic and Inorganic (NAICS 325510) CLIN 0005: Paints, Coatings, and Adhesives (NAICS 325510) CLIN 0006: Miscellaneous Hardware, Tools, and Gaskets (NAICS 332510) CLIN 0007: Other Class IX Sustainment Products SECTION C � CAAA RASP EXECUTION BUSINESS RULES 1. GENERAL RULES A BOA is not a contract (FAR 16.703(a)). An order becomes a binding contract upon Government acceptance and award. The ordering period shall not exceed five (5) years from initial execution (DFARS 216.703(c)). Each BOA will be formally reviewed by the PCO annually (FAR 16.703(c)(2)) and revised as necessary. BOAs shall be changed only by modifying the agreement itself, not by individual orders. Modifications do not apply retroactively to active orders. Prior to the annual review, the PCO will confirm in writing if the contractor wishes to maintain the agreement. Either party may elect not to renew. The Government may cancel the BOA at any time if in its best interest. Only the Army Contracting Command�Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA) is authorized to execute, modify, or perform annual reviews of these master BOAs. Other DoD activities may place orders under these BOAs with ACC-RIA approval. 2. STEP TWO EXECUTED BOAS (QUALIFICATION PHASE) Offerors must demonstrate technical capability in at least one (1) supply category listed in Attachment 0001- RASP BOA Purchase Description by completing Attachment 0004 � Combined Technical and Past Performance Questionnaire. No site visits are required at this stage. 3. STEP THREE ORDER REQUESTS (ORDERING PHASE) Order competitions are limited to active master BOA holders. Order performance periods will be established in each order and remain valid through completion, even if they extend beyond the master BOA's 5-year term. Specific evaluation criteria (e.g., Price-Only, LPTA, or Tradeoff) will be identified in each order RFQ. Detail PDs, TDPs, and QA requirements will be provided at the order level. All orders will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). Work shall not begin until the order is awarded. Business size standards and Non-Manufacturer Rule compliance will be certified and monitored at the order level. SECTION H � SPECIAL CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS 1. ALIGNMENT All supplies delivered under individual orders must support manufacturing and readiness at CAAA. Processes, tolerances, and quality controls must align with technical data packages (TDPs) provided at the order level. 2. JOINT CERTIFICAITON PROGRAM (JCP) Master BOA Level: To be eligible for a master BOA, and to maintain eligibility, the contractor must possess and maintain active JCP registration to access export-controlled TDPs and drawings. Verification: The Government will independently verify JCP status prior to execution. Failure to maintain active certification results in immediate termination of the BOA. Subcontractors: Prime contractors must ensure subcontractors are registered in the JCP if they require access to restricted drawings. Information Link: Procedures are available at the DLA Joint Certification Program (JCP) Website. 3. CYBERSECURITY MATURITY MODEL CERTIFICATION (CMMC) Conditional Self-Assessment: To be eligible for award, and to remain eligible for orders, the contractor must maintain at least a conditional CMMC Level 2 Self-Assessment in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) at award. Maintenance: Failure to maintain this status will result in immediate restriction from participating in order RFQs, inability to exercise options, and potential removal from the RASP BOA. Flow-Down: Subcontractor CMMC requirements (ranging from non-applicable to Level 2) will be defined in individual order solicitations. Primes are solely responsible for subcontractor compliance. 4. SUBCONTRACTING LIMITS AND THE NON-MANUFACTURER RULE (NMR) Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14): Primes must perform at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing (excluding materials) for supply orders. Non-Manufacturer Rule (FAR 52.219-33): Non-manufacturers must supply the product of a domestic small business manufacturer, unless an SBA class or individual waiver applies. The KO will monitor compliance at the order level. 5. LOCAL GATE SECURITY AND CAAA DELIVERY PROTOCOLS Delivery Address: CAAA, 300 Highway 361, Crane, IN 47522. Receiving Hours: 0700 to 1430, Monday through Thursday (excluding Holidays). By Appointment Only: Deliveries require a Carrier Appointm

description: Renovate Specialty Clinics 2nd Floor Project #517-22-202 All information required for submission is provided herein. There is no separate RFP package to download. NAICS: 541310 Architectural Services (Sector: Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services). PSC: C1DA Architect and Engineering Construction: Hospitals and Infirmaries. The Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC), HSA 1.3 Contracting, 200 Veterans Drive, Beckley, WV 25801, is soliciting Architect/Engineer (A/E) Services to provide Schematic Design, Life Cycle Cost Analysis (LCCA), Design Development, Construction and Bid Documents, Specifications, Construction Cost Estimates, and construction period services for the Renovate Specialty Clinics on 2nd Floor project at the Beckley VAMC, 200 Veterans Drive, Beckley, WV 25801. Set Aside This acquisition is a 100% Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set aside. Any subsequent award will require firms to be: Registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov; Visible and certified in the SBA Veteran Small Business Certification database at https://search.certifications.sba.gov; Compliant with VETS 4212 reporting at https://www.dol.gov/agencies/vets/programs/vets4212. No ZIP files. Receipt must be confirmed. SF 330s are due no later than 2:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on October 26, 2026. Your response shall follow the same order as the Evaluation Factors listed below. Failure to follow this format may result in rejection of the SF 330. The SF 330 form can be found on the GSA forms website at www.gsa.gov. All questions must be emailed to Millard.Adkins@va.gov no later than 2:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on October 14, 2026. Potential contractors must be registered in SAM (www.sam.gov), visible and certified in https://search.certifications.sba.gov, and compliant in VETS 4212 (https://www.dol.gov/agencies/vets/programs/vets4212) at the time of submission and at the time of award. Include an insert with the following: SAM UEI, Tax Identification Number, the email address and phone number of the primary point of contact, and a printed copy of the firm s SDVOSB certification/registry. Offerors shall provide all documents listed and comply with all instructions for their proposal to be considered responsive. Unverified SDVOSBs will be considered nonresponsive and will not be evaluated. General Information This is a Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business set aside. NAICS 541310; size standard $12.5 million. No solicitation package or bidder/plan holder list will be issued, and no solicitation documents are available. This procurement is subject to the availability of funds. The Government is under no obligation to award a contract because of this announcement. A/E Eligibility and Disciplines The selected A/E firm shall meet the FAR 2.101 definition of Architect engineer services as defined in 40 U.S.C. 1102 and FAR 36.6. The SDVOSB architectural firm must employ the principal Architect responsible for the design of this project and be heavily involved in all aspects of the design, including stamping drawings along with other team disciplines. A/Es signing drawings must be licensed; licenses are required at the time of award. Disciplines expected to be required: Architecture; Structural; Civil; Mechanical (HVAC); Plumbing; Electrical; Fire Protection; Industrial Hygiene; Interior Design; Surveying; Cost Estimating; Certified Physical Security Specialist; and other A/E services as defined by FAR 36.6 as necessary. Project Identification Renovate Specialty Clinics on 2nd Floor Project No. 517 22 202 A/E SCOPE OF WORK GENERAL: This project, Non-recurring Maintenance, will engage an architectural/engineering (A/E) firm to provide a complete design for a new renovation of our 2nd floor specialty and support space to create updated clinic spaces. This project would provide much needed improvements at the VA Beckley Campus. This project will require extensive assistance from the A/E interior designer as this is an area that is viewed heavily by Veterans, family, visitors, and staff throughout the day to day while in the building. Our facility presently does not have an interior designer on staff. Therefore, this will require the A/E interior designer to be heavily engaged with the VA staff throughout the entire process to achieve an aesthetically pleasing appearance to the 2nd floor. Although the project is for approximately 16,530 square feet on the 2nd, an all-inclusive concept will need to be created. This will lay the groundwork to provide a world class care setting for this hospital. This project will help reinforce the quality of care that our Veterans receive. The A/E would be expected to collaborate with other A/E firms involved in other projects throughout the facility. The renovation is anticipated to be extensive due to the building s original construction dating back to the 1950 s. Given its age, significant upgrades to all systems are expected to be necessary to meet current code, standards, and VA requirements. PURPOSE: The desired result is to provide improvements for approximately 16,530 square feet of specialty clinic space, located on the 2nd floor of BECVAMC Building 1. The renovation will provide our veterans with an updated central check-in and waiting area, improved wayfinding through updated layout, and improved traffic flows. It will also improve the clinic layout as the current clinic space was originally designed for medical surgical care. The 2nd floor has approximately 58,853 square feet that must be evaluated to determine the optimum location and layout for clinic space. The existing conditions for specialty clinics are spread over many floors of the hospital with hopes to bring or relocate most/many to the 2nd floor. This project would allow our facility to utilize a one-stop care approach by bringing services directly to our Veterans in their exam rooms. By creating correctly sized exam rooms it will help to accommodate the Veterans, their family, and caregivers who accompany them to their appointments. The design would also accommodate Veterans who use mobility scooters and larger wheelchairs. Veteran privacy will be enhanced by reducing foot and equipment traffic This project will renovate to provide space to meet VA guidelines. This project would establish a central check-in and waiting area for the 2nd floor clinics that would be easily accessible and accommodate Veterans and their caregivers. The waiting area would also improve efficiency and wayfinding, as well as increase Veteran satisfaction. LOCATION: Building 1, primarily on the 2nd floor of the VA Medical Center in Beckley, WV. PROJECT: This project includes but is not limited to the items listed below. The architect shall produce construction drawings for a full design encompassing all disciplines. Such as demolition and new construction, interiors, phasing plans for work, infection control plans, outages, mechanical and temporary access during construction, as well as furniture, fixtures, and equipment. VA Beckley has been approved for the renovation of the 2nd floor area and support space to create, expand clinics that will comply with VA guidelines. The architect shall verify and detail all utility moves and upgrades to support the renovation floorplans. title: Sources Sought/Request for Information Upper Mississippi River Restoration (UMRR) � Quincy Bay Habitat Rehabilitation and Enhancement Project- Stage 1
description: Sources Sought/Request for Information Upper Mississippi River Restoration (UMRR) � Quincy Bay Habitat Rehabilitation and Enhancement Project- Stage 1 Purpose and Objectives: The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of all qualified companies; (2) whether they are small or large businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service-disabled, veteran- owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; woman-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; and (3) their understanding and experience relative to the proposed acquisition to assist the Government in determining the expectation of receiving bids from responsible contractors at fair market prices. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set- aside is possible. An organization that is not under the applicable NAICS code can submit a response to this notice, however their capabilities may/may not be assessed for the purposes of this notice. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement as a set-aside based upon responses to this Notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Corps of Engineers (COE), Rock Island District does not intend to award a contract on the basis of responses received. This announcement is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as commitment by the Government, implied or otherwise, to issue a solicitation or make a contract award. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. This is NOT a request for proposal, quote or invitation for bid. Interested parties are expected to review this Notice and the Project Requirements to familiarize themselves with the requirements of this project. NAICS Code and Size Standard: In the event a solicitation is issued, North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction, with a size standard of $45 Million, is being considered. Solicitation Type: The Government is considering using a RFO FAR 14 Invitation for Bid for solicitation of this project. Background: The Quincy Bay Habitat Rehabilitation and Enhancement Project area spans approximately 2,350 acres along the right descending bank of the Upper Mississippi River System, situated between River Mile 327.0 to 332.0 within Pool 21. It is located in Adams County, Illinois adjacent to the City of Quincy. The project area contains several Mississippi River Project Master Plan land classifications, including Wildlife Management, High Density Recreation, and Vegetation Management land classifications. Historically, Quincy Bay was an important stopover point for diving ducks during spring and fall migrations. Sedimentation within the project area has resulted in decreased water depths and reduced habitat availability. Today, the reduced depth of the Upper Bay and lack of aquatic vegetation supports very few migratory waterfowl. Furthermore, floodplain forests have experienced an increase in invasive species and a decrease in regeneration and diversity. Relatively diverse pre-settlement floodplain forests are now largely dominated by silver maple and cottonwood. Without restoration, the project area�s open waters would continue to convert to shallow backwaters and drier bottomland forests would continue to develop into plant communities dominated by flood tolerant species and invasive species such as reed canary grass and Japanese hops. The entirety of the Quincy Bay Habitat Rehabilitation and Enhancement Project consists of the following proposed activities and features: dredged material placement with forest rehabilitation, dredging for overwintering habitat and sediment reduction, bank stabilization, river training structures, cut-through channel modification, Cedar Creek modification, vegetated overflow structures, aquatic vegetation plantings, timber stand improvement, and pothole enhancement. The total project will be carried out in multiple stages. The focus of this Sources Sought is Stage 1: dredging for overwintering habitat, access dredging, topographic diversity enhancement, bank stabilization, and river training structures. Project Requirements: Stage 1: Dredging for Overwintering Habitat (OW 1-3), Access Dredging (AD-OW-1 AD-OW-3), Topographic Diversity (TD 1-4), Bank Stabilization (BS 2), and River Training Structure (RTS 4-5) See Figure 1 for feature locations. Areas considered as part of this Project and described as the Project area include Quincy Bay, Quinsippi Island, backwater areas, and adjacent federally owned General Plan Lands. Approximately 16 acres of Quincy Bay and backwater channels will require access dredging (AD-OW-1 AD-OW-3), with approximately 19 acres requiring additional dredging to create deeper overwintering habitat (OW 1-3) for native species. Mechanical excavation/dredging will be required. Channel depths are up to 8 feet below flat pool and will have a channel bottom between 50 and 60 feet wide. Quantities excavated will be approximately 260,000 cubic yards of material over a total length approaching 16,000 feet. Excavated material will be side cast where possible and shaped to tie into the existing bankline. This material will be handled multiple times. Side casting will only be possible for a portion of the material to be removed from the dredge cuts. Material that cannot be side cast and shaped will need to be hauled to the shoreline placement sites. Placement sites are located at a minimum of 25 feet from the channel cut. The placement sites vary in width ranging from approximately 40 feet wide to 60 feet wide. Material will be required to remain within the placement site limits, with no material allowed to reenter the channel cuts, or be removed from the project area. These dredge placement sites will be used for topographic diversity features (TD 1-4). A top elevation may not be exceeded at the placement sites, and material will be required to be spread evenly across the placement sites in preparation for future work. Shaping of these sites to maintain a side slope will also be required. Tree/brush clearing will be required in select locations to ensure placement sites tie into the bankline. Trees outside of the placement site limits will not be damaged or removed. Bank stabilization (BS 2) for approximately 400 linear feet on Cedar Creek will require clearing; hauling, grading, and shaping; and placement of 1,100 tons of RR3 sized stone, with approximately 8 inches of bedding stone underlay. The bank will be shaped to maintain a predetermined slope to height ratio per the project design, with consideration for the width of the stone placement. Surveying after the bank stabilization to confirm the appropriate ratio will be required. River Training Structures (RTS 4-5) along the exterior edge of topographic diversity placement (TD1) will require specific shaping of dredged material to create more diversity in the placement alignment/orientation. This will be a construction contract to be primarily constructed during 2028. Capability Statement/Information Sought: All parties interested in this project must demonstrate that they would have the potential to be a responsive and responsible contractor. Interested businesses shall include the following information to be considered for this Sources Sought announcement: Company Name, UEI/CAGE (If your company does not have at the time of this sources sought, please be aware that you will be required to register your company in the System of Award Management (SAM) system to be eligible for any future Federal contracts), POC information including an email, current small business and socio-economic status for the NAICS code listed above. title: Ground Systems and Mission Operations-4 (GSMO-4)
description: This RFI is for informational purposes only. It is not a request for proposals or a solicitation for a contract or grant award and it does not obligate the Government in any way. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with responding to this request. Introduction The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is seeking information from qualified vendors capable of supporting science and Earth science missions including, but not limited to: Earth Observing System; Earth Observing System Data and Operations System; Magnetospheric Multi-Scale mission; Global Precipitation Measurement mission; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; James Webb Space Telescope; Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (built by NASA for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration); Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope; and Solar Dynamics Observatory. This RFI is intended to gather market intelligence, technical approaches, and rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) considerations to inform a potential future procurement. Background The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) currently acquires mission operations support through the Goddard Space Mission Operations (GSMO?3) contract. GSMO?3 provides comprehensive, end?to?end mission operations services spanning the entire mission life cycle. The scope of work includes systems and facility engineering; launch and early?orbit operations support; flight operations and flight dynamics services; sustaining engineering; and mission operations studies, design, integration, and testing of ground systems. Additional services include mission data collection and distribution, system administration, and information technology security and engineering analyses. The GSMO?3 contract supports a broad portfolio of NASA science and Earth science missions, including the Earth Observing System (EOS), Magnetospheric Multi?Scale (MMS), Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Fermi Gamma?ray Space Telescope, Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES), Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). These services are essential to sustaining and advancing NASA�s ground data systems and mission operations infrastructure, ensuring reliable communication, data processing, and mission control capabilities for ongoing and future missions. The contract also supports mission decommissioning and long?term sustaining engineering required to maintain operational readiness for systems with multidecade lifespans. The scope also increasingly encompasses cloud infrastructure management, continuous cybersecurity monitoring, DevSecOps automation, and advanced collision avoidance/conjunction assessment activities. Functions FUNCTION 1- Mission Ground System Support Services A. Ground Systems Engineering and Engineering Studies B. Ground Systems Support Services C. Ground Systems Integration and Test Services FUNCTION 2 - Mission Operations System Support Services A. Operations Systems Engineering B. Launch and Early Operations Support C. Flight Operations D. Flight Dynamics Support Services E. Mission Data Collection and Distribution F. Mission Systems Sustaining Engineering G. Systems Administration and IT Security H. Database Administration RFI Response Instructions The Government is seeking feedback from contractors with relevant mission capabilities and experience. Responses should include the vendor implementation approach and rough order magnitude costs of performing the functions listed below. Responses should be limited to no more than 30 pages. Transition from Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) to Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) The Government is evaluating the feasibility of transitioning the follow-on GSMO-4 requirement from a Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contract to a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract, either in whole or in part, including the use of Performance Based Payments for FFP Tasks. The Government seeks industry feedback regarding the practicality of such an approach. Specifically, respondents are requested to address the following: Is the current GSMO-4 scope sufficiently defined and stable to support an FFP contract? If not, identify the areas of uncertainty. What technical, programmatic, schedule, or cost risks would your organization associate with transitioning this requirement from CPAF to FFP? Which portions of the requirement, if any, do you believe are well-suited for FFP, and which portions would be more appropriately performed under another contract type (e.g., Time-and-Materials)? Please explain your rationale. What assumptions or Government-provided information (e.g., historical workload, staffing profiles, performance metrics, technical baseline, service level agreements, demand forecasts, configuration data) would be necessary for your organization to develop a realistic fixed-price proposal? What contract incentives or performance metrics would improve the viability of an FFP approach? What acquisition or contract structure would best balance cost control, performance, innovation, and risk allocation for this requirement? Please identify any lessons learned or best practices from similar transitions from Cost-Reimbursement to Firm-Fixed-Price contracts. Are there specific contract provisions or performance requirements that should be modified to enable a successful transition to FFP? Catalog Pricing Structure: The Government is exploring a 'Catalog-style' pricing structure for routine Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) operations, where missions are priced based on their Risk Classification (e.g., Class B, C, D). What are the benefits, risks, and potential cost-drivers your firm would associate with pricing mission operations by Class? What specific parameters, boundaries, or Service Level Agreements (SLAs) would be required in the catalog definitions to make this pricing model viable. Core vs. IDIQ Structure: The Government is considering a contract structure that establishes highly stable, long-term flagship missions as the baseline 'Core' requirement, with all other missions and development efforts issued as IDIQ task orders. How would this Core-plus-IDIQ structure impact your pricing, workforce retention, and risk allocation strategies compared to a 100% IDIQ structure. Requirements/Specifications Available Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Resources: The Government maintains operations resources listed below. RFI responses may include the use of these GFE resources. For any GFE resources incorporated in their response, the vendor should include any GSMO implementation costs and the cost differences/savings as compared to the vendor providing all ground resources.

The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor

The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. title: Combined Synopsis / Solicitation for a potential Supply Chain Management Contract for F108 Engine Support � Mission Analysis
description: This notice serves as DLA Weapon Support�s combined synopsis/solicitation as described in FAR 12.603, in accordance with FAR 5.201, and the approved J&A under authority of FAR 6.103-1 and 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), for addition of KC/RC/WC135 Mission Analysis for the CFM56-2 Engine, F108 Model Updates, and an F108 Self-Locking Borescope Plug set certification. This effort is anticipated to be made as an addition to sole source Long Term Contract SPE4AX-25-D-9406 to CFM International Inc. (CFM), Contractor and Government Entity (CAGE) code 58828. This is a FAR part 12 effort being added to the current contract SPE4AX-25-D-9406. KC/RC/WC135 Mission Analysis, F108 Model Updates, and Borescope certification support services for the United States Air Force (USAF) are being solicited to be added to contract SPE4AX-25-D-9406, awarded to CFM International Inc. CAGE 58828. Actual requirements for the additional scope will be negotiated and added to the basic contract. Individual requirements are certified as sole source to CFM and synopsized in accordance with FAR 5.201. DLA Weapons Support will issue a letter solicitation (RFP) to the sole source Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). If any non-OEM source is interested in providing the entire support for this effort, please notify the Contracting Officer prior to the combined synopsis/solicitation closing date. A copy of the letter of interest should be forwarded to the Contracting Officer identified herein. The Government may alter the acquisition strategy if it is in the best interest of the Government. In order to receive an award, the contractor must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). SAM registration is at https://www.sam.gov. It is anticipated that this requirement will be added as a separate line item to the current sole source CFM COI contract SPE4AX-25-D-9406. The data required to perform the necessary services is CFM�s proprietary and confidential commercial intellectual data and cannot be shared or provided by the Government. Only sources with access to the F108 series of engines performance information will be considered as a qualified source. The scope of work is as follows: 1. KC/RC/WC135 Mission Analysis for the CFM56-2 Engine � The contractor shall define the mission characteristics and all variants that the KC135, RC135 and WC135 aircraft fly. The contractor shall assess the validity of engine usage assumptions made during engine certification and, by extension, the Life Limited Part (LLP) Low Cycle Fatigue (LCF) limitations and maintenance intervals published by CFMI. Since 1985, the KC135, RC135 and WC135 have been operating with the CFM56-2 engines as powerplants. In that time there have been several efforts accomplished by CFMI to verify the flight characteristics of the mission established for these weapon systems. The last assessment was accomplished in 2015, for high pressure system components and drove some changes to LLP lives. Since it has been a significant amount of time since the last assessment, another mission analysis is recommended to determine if the flight characteristics have changed significantly to impact life limits and maintenance intervals. The contractor shall perform all necessary tasks required to complete an assessment as described above. Using flight data provided by the Air Force and pilot interviews taken by CFMI, analysis will be conducted to establish the mission characteristics and possible impact to cycle definition, LLP limits and maintenance intervals. Once the contractor has completed the needed analysis and evaluation of the current KC/RC/WC135 missions, they will submit findings and results through their internal review process. Successful review will then drive a report for the Air Force that defines the mission characteristics along with a comparative review of the Air Force�s current mission versus previous mission. These results will be provided in a report to the USAF for USAF review and assessment. 2. F108 Model Updates � The contractor shall update thermal, CAD and stress F108 part models to prepare for future use during lifing analysis, field investigations, design tasks or other program needs. Thermal and stress analyses may be required to support lifing analysis following mission analysis updates; thermal and stress analyses may also be required in the future to support new field investigations or hardware redesign tasks. Multiple variants may need to be analyzed. Current models were constructed utilizing legacy tools (Patran, PThermal, Flow Network Solver). These models need to be transitioned to the current production tool set by passing them through the model conversion and upgrade process. This will convert them to Next-Gen Thermal & Flow Simulator. Modifications may be necessary to facilitate this process and ensure that converted model results align with legacy results within acceptable tolerances. Once this process is deemed successful, then additional model variants may be constructed. Upon completion of this, thermal and stress analyses can be performed. The contractor shall provide a memorandum confirming successful model updates to the USAF for USAF review and assessment. 3. F108 Self-Locking Borescope Plug set certification � The contractor shall provide a full self-locking borescope plug certification with a service bulletin release that approves the self-locking borescope plug set with a new auto-locking feature, eliminating the need for safety wire. The service bulletin will approve this new design, for us on the CFM56-2B engine configuration (USAF ref F108). The US Air Force F108 engine fleet has experienced breakages of the borescope plugs which can lead to FOD damage and presents a challenging effort to remove the broken pieces. These breakages are manifested in the 3 borescope plugs located at the stage 7, stage 8 and stage 9 positions of the high pressure compressor. Along with the breakages of these 3 plugs, all borescope plugs require safety wire as a redundant feature to ensure the plugs are locked in place. This results in extensive and unnecessary mission downtime as well as maintenance time to complete the laborious task of applying safety wire to all the plugs. The new self-locking borescope plug set consists of 15 new borescope plug assemblies that incorporate a new self-locking feature, which eliminates the requirement for safety wire. The new plug design also employs a more robust design for the compressor plugs at stage 7, stage 8 and stage 9 which eliminates the cause of breakages. So, the new borescope plug set reduces maintenance time as it eliminates the need for safety wire and reduces failures with a stronger plug at the vulnerable areas. The contractor shall perform all necessary tasks required to achieve certification of the Self Locking borescope plug set used on the CFM56-2 engines (USAF F108) and release a service bulletin documenting the approved application of this borescope plug set for use on the CFM56-2 engine configuration. Both the Original Engine Manufacturer (OEM) and the Air Force have experience with this type of self-locking design. However, the experience is on engines that have a different mission profile and the parts in use are not borescope plugs. It is necessary to have the engine manufacturer perform all necessary reviews and analysis to verify and validate the application of the borescope plug set on the CFM56-2 engine fleet. title: Request for Information _ Creation of The United States Space Academy
description: On Aug. 28, 2026, President Donald J. Trump issued Executive Order (E.O.) 14423, Establishing the United States Space Academy. To answer that call, the United States Space Academy (USSA) is envisioned as a NASA-led, civilian Federal academic institution that combines rigorous technical education with disciplined leadership development, civic responsibility, and a lasting commitment to public service. The Academy will prepare future scientists, engineers, astronauts, pilots, operators, entrepreneurs, civil servants, warfighters, and other leaders to advance American interests across the aerospace sector. Through this Request for Information (RFI), NASA invites each State to submit one official State-sponsored response prepared by a �Responding Entity� and coordinated and formally endorsed by a State Selecting Official. The Governor must designate both the Responding Entity and the State Selecting Official in writing. The response should provide information to support NASA�s assessment of potential locations and operating solutions for the United States Space Academy (USSA). That assessment will inform NASA�s recommendation to the Commission. NASA�s objectives for this announcement are to: Identify potential locations for the permanent establishment of the USSA campus, including a groundbreaking no later than 2027. Identify interim solutions that may allow the USSA to begin instruction in 2028 and facilitate a smooth transition to a permanent campus by 2031. Explore the estimated costs of establishing the USSA and potential state, local, and other non-Federal partnerships that could support its establishment. Information obtained through this RFI will be used by NASA and the Commission to develop the recommended process for selecting the Academy�s permanent physical location, which will be reported to the President for decision. A separate announcement for formal proposals may be issued at a later date.

title: Secondo tubo San Gottardo (2TG Röhre Nord und Galleria di Airolo) und N2 Risanamento primo tubo San Gottardo (1TG Röhre Süd) Lot 1002 – Energieverteilung
description:
Afin de permettre la rénovation du tunnel routier du Gothard existant, long d'environ 17 km, le Conseil fédéral, le Parlement et la population ont décidé de construire un deuxième tube. L'équipement EES du deuxième tube, appelé tube nord, sera réalisé entre 2027 et 2030, en partie parallèlement à l'achèvement des travaux de construction du génie civil. Parallèlement au tube nord, la Galleria di Airolo (GdA), d'une longueur d'environ 1 km, sera également réalisée et fera partie intégrante du système du Gothard.

Immédiatement après l'ouverture du tube nord en circulation bidirectionnelle, la rénovation du tube existant, appelé tube sud, sera effectuée. La rénovation génie civil est prévue entre 2030 et 2033. L'équipement EES existant du tube sud sera entièrement démantelé en raison de son âge. La réalisation du nouvel équipement EES se fera en partie parallèlement à l'exploitation du trafic et devrait durer jusqu'en 2036. À terme, le GTG fonctionnera en sens unidirectionnel (une voie plus une bande d'arrêt d'urgence par tube) à une vitesse de 80 km/h. Cependant, la fermeture d'un tube sera régulièrement nécessaire pour des raisons d'entretien ou en cas d'incident.

 

 

Le présent lot comprend:

La réalisation, les contrôles, la livraison et le montage des tableaux de distribution BT pour les tubes Nord et Sud ainsi que pour la Galleria di Airolo.

title: Udførelse af sporgasmålinger (total metanemission) samt landbrugsfaglig rådgivning
description: Dette udbud omhandler deltagelse i projektet DOMETEK under ledelse af Danmarks Tekniske Universitet (DTU). Projektet udføres af DTU med deltagelse af flere underleverandører og løber frem til ultimo april, 2029. Formålet med projektet er at dokumentere metanemissionen på bedriftsniveau (stald + lager), når disse tiltag implementeres, med tilstrækkelig præcision og robusthed til at blive inkluderet i Danmarks nationale emissionsopgørelse. Emissionsmålingerne udføres over et fuldt kalenderår, så dokumentationen inkluderer relevante sæsonvariationer og driftsforhold, afspejler bedriftspraksis og sikrer overførbarhed til national skala. I projektet bestemmes absolutte metanemissioner fra bedrifter med henholdsvis hyppig udslusning (ny referencepraksis), bioforgasning af gylle og forsuring af gylle, der repræsenterer modne teknologier udviklet, testet og implementeret på danske grisebedrifter, hvorved reduktionspotentialet for fuldskala anvendelse opnås. I alt udføres 240 emissionsmålinger på 40 grisebedrifter, der dækker tre bedriftspraksisser. Der anvendes udelukkende sporgasmålinger ("TDM metoden") til bestemmelse af metanemission. Projektets hovedresultater er årlige metanemissionsrater,emissionsfaktorer og reduktionseffektiviteter, der er repræsentative for de tre bedriftspraksisser. Denne leverance ("delkontrakt 1") omfatter: - Udførelse af sporgasmålinger til bestemmelse af total metanemission fra 10 bedrifter med 6 målinger fordelt over et kalenderår (60 målinger). - Landbrugsfaglig rådgivning - herunder: Udvælgelse af bedrifter til måling af metanemission samt indhenting af data fra gårde om bedriftsstørrelse mv., vurdering af sæson og døgnvariation i metanemission og bestemmelse af metan emissionsfaktorer.

title: Germany – Engineering services – Sanierung Verwaltungsgebäude II, Emden / Fachplanung - Tragwerk (Denkmalschutz)
description: Gegenstand des Vergabeverfahrens sind Fachplanungsleistungen der Tragwerksplanung gemäß Teil 4 Abschnitt 1 der Honorarordnung für Architekten und Ingenieure (HOAI) für die umfassende Sanierung des denkmalgeschützten Verwaltungsgebäude II der Stadt Emden. Der Auftrag umfasst sämtliche für die Umsetzung der Gesamtmaßnahme erforderlichen Leistungen der Tragwerksplanung. Hierzu gehören insbesondere die Untersuchung und Bewertung des baulichen Bestands, die statische Beurteilung vorhandener Tragkonstruktionen sowie die Entwicklung technisch, wirtschaftlich und denkmalgerecht abgestimmter Sanierungskonzepte. Darüber hinaus sind alle im Rahmen der Planung und Ausführung erforderlichen Nachweise, Berechnungen, Abstimmungen und Beratungsleistungen zu erbringen, die für eine fachgerechte und genehmigungsfähige Umsetzung der Maßnahme notwendig sind.

title: Malta – Event services – Provision of Event Organization Services for Administrative and Operational Meetings and Events for the EUAA
description: EUAA envisages awarding up to three (3) framework service contracts in cascade for each Lot for the provision of high-quality Event Organisation Services and related travel and logistical services required for the organisation and implementation of the Agency's administrative and operational meetings and events. The framework contracts will support events organised in Moldova (Lot 1), Ukraine (Lot 2) and the Western Balkans (Lot 3), as further described in the Technical specifications. The services to be provided under the framework contracts will depend on the specific requirements of each event, as defined by the Agency. They may include, but are not limited to: • Conference venue rental; • Provision of audio-visual (AV) and interpretation equipment; • Catering services; • Coordination of third-party service providers and on-site logistical management; • Preparation of event signage and submission of supporting documents and invoices, where required; • Rental of AV and interpretation equipment for venues provided by the Agency, stakeholders or other third parties; • Organisation of lunches, dinners and other catering arrangements; • Reservation of suitable accommodation in accordance with the Agency's requirements; • Organisation, provision and supervision of transportation services; • Provision of event assistance services before, during and after the event; • Coordination and provision of security and medical services, where required; • Processing and payment of travel, accommodation and/or subsistence allowances for event participants, including the collection of the relevant supporting documents, in accordance with the Agency's instructions. Events in Ukraine will only be organised where the prevailing security situation allows the Agency to hold in-person events, following the Agency's security assessment and any applicable security restrictions.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Planungsleistung TGA HLS - ALG 1, 2, 3, 8 - Erweiterung Hauptfeuerwache Potsdam, 14467 Potsdam
description: Der Fachbereich 37 der Landeshauptstadt Potsdam, hier Feuerwehr, benötigt einen Neubau, mit zweigeschossigem Verbinder/Laufgang, zur Bestandswache, auf dem Gelände zwischen Holzmarktstraße und Türkstraße in 14467 Potsdam. Im Zuge einer vorgelagerten Machbarkeitsstudie, wurde der benötigte Bedarf ermittelt und maximale Baugrößen und Randbedingungen identifiziert, mit den beteiligten Ämtern vorabgestimmt und durch diese schriftlich freigegeben. Im Zuge der Planung sollen jedoch noch 3 verschiedene Ansichten der Fassadengestaltung der Denkmalbehörde zur Abstimmung vorgelegt werden. Genehmigungsfähig ist ein Gebäude mit bis zu 4 Geschossen und einer maximalen Höhe von 15 m einschließlich aller technischen Aufbauten. Die ersten beiden Geschosse sind als Parkebene zu planen. Besonderheit im EG ist die benötigte Durchfahrtshöhe von 4,0 m. Gegenstand der Planung sind TGA-Leistungen nach HOAI für die Anlagengruppen Wasser/Abwasser, Wärmeversorgung, Lüftung und Gebäudeautomation.

title: Weinfelden and Müllheim Hydropower Plants – General Planning Services
description:
The subject of the procurement is the interdisciplinary general planning services for the further design and implementation of the Weinfelden and Müllheim hydropower plants in the Canton of Thurgau.


The procurement is carried out jointly by Wasserkraftwerke Weinfelden AG, Thurkraftwerk AG and Isento Wasserkraft AG.


The mandate includes, in particular, the construction of the new hydropower plants, the restoration of fish passage, hydraulic engineering works, the dismantling of existing power plants and canal facilities, as well as the restoration of the affected areas and watercourses.


The procurement comprises two project lots:

  • Lot 1 – Weinfelden Hydropower Plant: Contracting authority Wasserkraftwerke Weinfelden AG, general planning services for phases 32–53
  • Lot 2 – Müllheim Hydropower Plant: Contracting authorities Thurkraftwerk AG and Isento Wasserkraft AG, general planning services for phases 31–53


Applications and tenders must cover both project lots. It is intended to award both project lots to the same general planner. A separate general planning contract will be concluded for each project lot.

title: Sweden – Port operation services – Stuveri- och logistiktjänster
description: Upphandlingen avser stuveri-, maskin- och krantjänster samt tillhörande logistiktjänster i Hargs Hamn, Östhammars kommun. Uppdraget omfattar lossning och lastning av fartyg, hantering av gods inom hamnområdet, lossning och lastning av lastbilar, samt löpande skötsel av hamnområdet inklusive bl.a. snöröjning. Hamnen hanterar bulkgods med huvudsaklig inriktning på energiråvara, spannmål, skrot, träpellets och rundvirke, med en årlig godsvolym om cirka 640 000–800 000 ton. Projektlaster förekommer utöver fasta flöden av bulkgods. Avtalsperioden omfattar 2 år med möjlighet till förlängning i ytterligare 2 perioder om 2 år vardera, totalt upp till 6 år. Start 2027-07-01. Upphandlingen genomförs som ett öppet förfarande enligt lagen (2016:1146) om upphandling inom försörjningssektorerna (LUF). Kompletterande upphandlingsdokument nr 1 har publicerats 2026-09-15, det innehåller ändringar i utvärderingsmodellen och i avtalshandlingarna, Bilaga B och Bilaga G har ersatts av rättade versioner och anbud ska lämnas på dessa, och anbudstiden är förlängd till den 26 oktober.
